---------
th Order No. 02/Dated: 12 June, 2024 Heard learned counsel for the parties.

The petitioner has been made an accused in connection with Ahilyapur P.S. Case No. 47 of 2023 corresponding to Cyber Case No. 03 of 2024 registered for the offence under Sections 411, 414, 419,
420, 467, 468, 471, 120B/34 of the I.P.C. and Sections 66(B), 66(C), 66(D), of the Information Technology Act., pending in the Court of learned Special Judge Cyber Crime-Cum-Additional Sessions Judge-II, Giridih.

entities.text: Special Judge Cyber Crime-Cum-Additional Sessions Judge-II, Giridih
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: As per FIR, allegation is that on 18.12.2023, informant, Md. Musha, A.S.I. received an information that in house of the Nageshwar Mandal at Ghasco village of Ahilyapur Police Station area, some miscreants had gathered to commit Cyber fraud by making serial call to Bank/ATM customers without any fear and using social engineering in the name of blocking and verifying ATM cards.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that petitioner is innocent and has committed no offence at all as alleged in the FIR.

Petitioner undertakes to cooperate in the trial of the case by remaining physically present as and when required and shall not indulge in any manner in tampering with the prosecution evidences or influencing the witnesses of prosecution.
Hence, the petitioner may be extended the privilege of bail.
Petitioner is in the Judicial Custody since 05.03.2024.

Co-accused with similar allegations have already been extended privilege of bail by Co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 27.02.2024 passed in B.A. No. 10463 of 2023 and passed in B.A. No. 10356 of 2023.
Hence, the petitioner may be extended the privilege of bail.
Page 1|2
On the other hand, learned Addl.P.P appearing for the State has opposed the prayer for bail of the petitioner.
Hence, petitioner does not deserve bail.
